source.title: Capability Emergence Can Be Forecast: Per-Seed, In Advance, With Calibrated Intervals, Certified False Alarms, and a Blind Pre-Registered Gate

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study measures induction-related circuit scores and copying behavior over training, and tests whether precursor signals forecast induction emergence. It uses a forecasting protocol rather than reproducing the original mechanistic analysis.
record.gate_note: The study also discusses results from other work; those cited results are not recorded as rows. Grokking experiments are not about the claim. The study does not directly test head composition or whether induction heads carry most general in-context or few-shot learning.
record.test_reason: The study tracks previous-token scores, prefix-matching (induction) scores and copy advantage on repeated sequences over training. It does this in Pythia, OLMo-1 and OLMo-2 checkpoints and in its own two-layer seed fleets, with data-ablated, one-layer and trap-language controls and learning-rate and batch changes. The results bear on abrupt emergence (V2), universality (V4), dependence on data and setup (V5) and precursor-then-induction ordering (V7). They bear on V1 only indirectly, through the two-layer requirement and the precursor preceding induction. The paper's main contribution is a forecasting protocol; those method-performance numbers are not tests of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with one omission. The record does not say that the bare previous-token precursor fails in a pair-context trap language (10/10 false alarms) and must be conjoined with a graded behavioural signal. Authors also state frontier applicability and the cause of the ~0.84 fraction are not established.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses previous-token and induction measurements in forecasting experiments rather than reproducing the original induction-head mechanistic analysis; it adds per-seed event forecasts, negative controls, conformal intervals, and blind gates.
record.method_sensitivity: The precursor's false-alarm behavior depends on the language and whether previous-token context itself pays for the task: it has 0/10 false alarms in the bigram negatives but 10/10 in the trap-language blocked runs. Data ablation and architectural blocking also change the precursor/capability outcome. Learning rate and batch size change the precursor-to-event gap; the paper reports fixed offsets as timescale-local.
record.problems: The language-model evidence is limited to one capability, small synthetic fleets and public checkpoints (≤1B public suites as stated in the limitations). The fixed-configuration event-time spread only cleared its pre-registered bar by 0.01. The study does not directly test head composition, the claimed training-loss bump, general ICL, or few-shot learning. Some public-checkpoint timing is limited by checkpoint granularity.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported results were omitted. Figure-only trajectories without textually stated values were not transcribed as numeric rows.

untested.parts: Head composition (K/Q composition with the previous-token head) is not tested. The models are not stated to be attention-only. Copy advantage measures the [A][B]…[A]→[B] behaviour, but the circuit is not traced.
Co-occurrence with a bump in the training loss curve is not tested. General in-context learning (loss by token index) is not measured; only copy advantage on repeated random sequences.
Other architectures and modalities are not tested. Public models are limited to ≤1B-parameter suites per the limitations.
Effects of data and setup on whether in-context learning persists late in training are not tested.
Only a two-step ordering (previous-token head, then induction or copying) is resolved. Finer sub-steps or overlapping transitions are not examined.

missing.what: All five Pythia suites, which share batch and context configuration, cliff at the same ~2.1B tokens, consistent with configuration-determined timing.

Earlier trap-language designs: in an unlearnable language the precursor had no incentive; a too-rich language starved induction past the training budget. Data structure affects whether induction forms in budget.
A pure bigram language is solvable through the embedding pathway, so previous-token attention forms only where repetition exists.

record.verdict_notes: The grokking half of the paper (466 runs) is not about induction heads and is ignored. Many rows are forecasting-method performance and are set to none. A previous-token head forming before the induction head is itself described by Olsson et al. Its support for V7 is a two-step ordering, not a challenge to V2's abruptness of the induction head itself. Fleet architecture (attention-only or not) is unstated, which weakens the links to V1. Not peer reviewed.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures previous-token and induction scores and copying behavior, but does not directly test composition between heads or establish the detailed [A][B] … [A] → [B] attention-and-copy circuit.
It reports timing of induction-related scores and copy behavior, but does not establish that a bump in the training loss curve occurs at the same point.
The study does not measure later-token loss relative to earlier-token loss in large transformers or whether induction heads carry most general in-context learning.
It tests several language-model families, sizes, and settings, but not other architectures or modalities, nor universality across model families and training runs generally.
It tests dependence on selected data and training settings, not the full range of data and training setups.
The study does not test few-shot task learning or compare induction heads with other mechanisms as carriers of few-shot learning.
It shows a precursor preceding the measured induction/copying event, but does not resolve the full formation process into a detailed series of internal sub-steps.

rows.subject: Pythia suites (5; 70m/160m/410m, standard and deduped)
rows.operation_detail: Measured maximum early-layer previous-token score across checkpoints.
rows.note: Reported as a precursor score at the checkpoint before the capability cliff.
rows.check: Pythia is not a small attention-only model, so this row does not bear on V1. The precursor value marks a sub-step, not the V2 phase change itself.

source_check.correct: Absolute baseline not stated; 0.37 is approximately 10 times baseline. V7 observed; V4 cannot_determine from a previous-token score alone.
source_check.problem: The baseline field contains a comparison factor; the precursor score does not itself measure induction behaviour under V4.

rows.subject: Pythia suites (5; 70m/160m/410m, standard and deduped)
rows.operation_detail: Measured behavioral copy advantage on repeated random sequences.
rows.note: The paper describes the capability as still below its later cliff at this stage.
rows.check: Pre-cliff baseline for R4. Near-zero copy advantage while the precursor is already up is what V2 and V7 expect, so 'absent' mislabels it. Not V1 (not attention-only).

rows.subject: Pythia suites (5; 70m/160m/410m, standard and deduped)

rows.note: The paper says induction and copy advantage cliff at the following stage.
rows.check: Pre-cliff baseline for R5 (induction 0.019 one stage before 0.93). Not an absence of the effect. Not V1.

rows.check: Not V1: Pythia is not small or attention-only. The jump happens within one public-checkpoint stage, so window width is bounded by checkpoint granularity.

rows.operation_detail: Compared the precursor alarm with a best-case loss-threshold alarm.

rows.subject: Pythia-70m
rows.operation_detail: Measured induction score late in training.
rows.note: The study reports a partial late-training loss of induction.
rows.check: 'Reversed' overstates it. Induction score fell 0.93→0.36 at 67B tokens but did not vanish. This applies to pythia-70m only, not all suites.

source_check.correct: V4 observed: induction behaviour remains at score 0.36 after falling from 0.93. Partial regression is a description of score retention; V4 does not require persistence at peak strength.

rows.operation_detail: Compared valid anchor time with emergence time across runs.

rows.note: Aggregate over 80 valid-anchor runs.

rows.subject: Two-layer transformers (gap-origin study)
rows.operation_detail: Changed learning rate or batch size and measured the precursor-to-event gap.

rows.note: The authors report that neither optimization axis leaves the fixed offset unchanged.

rows.subject: Two-layer transformers (blind gap-law gate; 5 fresh seeds)
rows.operation_detail: Applied the frozen multiplicative interval based on precursor time.
rows.measure: interval coverage, events, false alarms, and observed multipliers

rows.value: 5/5 coverage; 5/5 events; 0 false alarms on fresh negatives; observed multipliers 1.160–1.226
rows.note: Blind validation of the multiplicative rule at a third never-seen configuration.
rows.check: Blind validation of the forecasting envelope measures method performance.
